SEBoK Organizational Roles and Responsibilities, Distilled

Fifth-batch SEBoK distillation, batch 4/5. The prompt-named URL Organizational_Roles_and_Responsibilities 404s; the discipline's dominant carrier is Organizing Business and Enterprises to Perform Systems Engineering (Part 5, lead authors Beasley/Pyster/Sillitto), with Roles and Competencies (SE-033) and Organizational Structures and Roles (SE-138) as adjacent carriers. The page enumerates five organizational structures (project, functional, matrix, integrated, product-centered) and three role-typologies (Sheard 1996 twelve roles; Sheard 2000 discovery-vs-program phase; Kasser et al. 2009 five SE types at increasing abstraction/ambiguity/scope/innovation; Sillitto 2011a). The article supplies a cleaner Cluster A universal-sibling lattice at the organization-structure rung (N=5) and a multi-rung Cluster B reading: roles compose at the within-organization rung (Beasley structures), the role-typology rung (Sheard, Kasser, Sillitto), and the SE-discipline rung (SE-033 / SE-138). Cluster C architectural school at the structure-choice rung (each structure carries a school's stance on where SE authority lives); Cluster K V3-as-procedure-binding at the role-and-responsibility-formalization rung; Cluster H hypostatic-boundary at the role-vs-person distinction.

II. Source Read

Lead authors Richard Beasley, Art Pyster, Hillary Sillitto. Part 5 > Enabling Systems Engineering > Enabling Businesses and Enterprises. Verbatim: businesses and enterprises are entities with "sufficiently strong central authority and motivation to take steps to enable SE"; infostructure is the "information infrastructure supporting the system lifecycle, including process libraries, modeling tools, shared workspaces, and IT facilities." Five organizational structures: (1) project organization (projects manage all resources/staffing), (2) functional organization (delegate to specialized functional groups), (3) matrix organization (SE professionals with home-base between projects), (4) integrated organization (SE tasks performed without specific functional allegiance), (5) product-centered organization (structure mirrors system breakdown structure with integrated product teams). Role-typologies: Sheard (1996) twelve SE roles; Sheard (2000) discovery-phase (high uncertainty) vs program-phase (deterministic); Kasser et al. (2009) five SE types at increasing levels of abstraction, ambiguity, scope, and innovation; Sillitto (2011a) various SE roles within engineering and business landscapes. Adjacent: SE-033 Roles and Competencies, SE-138 Organizational Structures and Roles, SE-157 Competency Assessment.

III. Structural Read

Cluster A universal-sibling lattice (Doc 572 D), at the organization-structure rung, N=5. Project / functional / matrix / integrated / product-centered is a clean N=5 universal-sibling lattice: every SE-performing organization adopts one structure (or composes hybrids) along the same axis. The axis discriminates by where SE authority lives (project-internal, function-internal, matrix-shared, integrated-into-engagement, product-line-bound). Convergent with the §VII.7 N≈10 marker as a sub-canonical N=5 reading.

Cluster B multi-keeper composition, vertical-extension sub-form (§VII.7 candidate). The Beasley structures + Sheard role-typologies + Kasser SE-types is a three-rung vertical Cluster B composition: organization-structure rung (where SE lives), role-typology rung (which roles SE-performers occupy), discipline-typology rung (which kind of SE-performer they are). The vertical-composition extension (SE-152 PfM-SE-PM keeper triplet, §VII.7 candidate) gains a second clean instance: organization-structure → role-type → discipline-type as an ascending-rung keeper triplet. Promotes the vertical-composition candidate from one to two instances.

Cluster C architectural school (Doc 538), at the structure-choice rung. Each of the five organizational structures carries a school's stance on SE authority: project-organization-school treats SE as project-resourced; functional-school treats SE as a discipline that lends specialists; matrix-school is the school of dual-allegiance; integrated-school is post-allegiance; product-centered-school binds SE to product-line lifecycle. Five schools at one decision-rung. Cluster C density grows; the school-pairing-types (engineering-engineering at SE-026, engineering-engagement at SE-037, engineering-non-engineering at SE-117) gain a fourth pairing: school-vs-school-within-discipline (where the schools all claim SE authority but locate it differently). Worth flagging.

Cluster K V3-as-procedure-binding, role-formalization mode. Roles and responsibilities exist as procedural binding because the discipline cannot rely on virtue (clarity-of-authority, hand-off-discipline) alone in a multi-keeper organization. The Beasley/Sheard/Kasser typologies are V3-shaped: name the role explicitly so the responsibility cannot be silently absorbed or rankism-distorted. V3 sub-mode: role-binding, candidate eighth sub-mode after gate-binding (SE-185) and evidential-binding (SE-186).

Cluster H hypostatic-boundary, role-vs-person. The role-typology discipline preserves the role-vs-person distinction: Sheard's twelve roles are roles, not people; one person can hold multiple roles, one role can be held by multiple people. The discipline names the functional surface (what the role does) without claiming the person IS the role. Hypostatic-boundary at the role rung.

Cluster J D8 dispersed-instrument with internal-migration. SE-187's discipline lives across SE-033 + SE-138 + SE-157 + the carrier page. This is internal-migration mode (per §VII.7 four-mode taxonomy: bidirectional-fold / internal-migration / external-migration / dual-discipline-distribution). SE-187 is an internal-migration instance.

V. Residuals

Editorial 404 reads as internal-migration. The discipline's formalization rung migrated into SE-033 + SE-138 + the Beasley carrier; SEBoK has no anchor article for the responsibility-and-role topic specifically. This is structurally distinct from SE-184's external-carrier (D8.1) reading and from SE-186's three-carrier dispersion: SE-187 is internal-migration only.
